strings.name: Moon Jae-in
strings.role: Former president of South Korea and human rights lawyer
strings.summary: Moon Jae-in entered politics after working as a human rights and labour lawyer in Busan. He served as a senior aide to Roh Moo-hyun and a lawmaker before becoming president from 2017 to 2022. He pursued inter-Korean dialogue and labour reform, meeting Kim Jong-un and signing declarations in 2018; signing did not itself achieve peace or denuclearization. After office he became involved in Pyeongsan Bookstore and public debate. Indicted for alleged bribery in 2025, he remains involved in ongoing court proceedings.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 18 November 2026. Recent activity is documented by an 18 September speech and 10 November visit to Gunsan; judicial developments are updated through the 17 November pretrial report. Election and inauguration, agreements and implementation, bookstore volunteering and corporate governance, allegations, responses and future trial arrangements are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: As South Korea’s former president, he promoted dialogue on the Korean Peninsula; his social reforms and foreign policy influenced Northeast Asian relations.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and legal education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Geoje, South Gyeongsang Province, on 24 January 1953. He graduated in law from Kyung Hee University and passed the judicial examination in 1980, beginning legal practice in Busan in 1982. His LL.B., examination and subsequent professional training are distinct qualifications, not a doctorate.
strings.facts.f2.label: From presidential aide to party leader
strings.facts.f2.value: He was senior presidential secretary for civil affairs in 2003–2004 and 2005–2006, responsible for civic and social affairs in 2004–2005, and Roh Moo-hyun’s chief of staff in 2007–2008. He helped prepare the 2007 inter-Korean summit. In 2015 he led the New Politics Alliance for Democracy and its renamed successor, the Democratic Party of Korea. These are historical positions.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Phased reform of working hours
strings.highlights.h1.text: On 28 February 2018 parliament amended the Labour Standards Act to reduce the generally applicable weekly maximum from 68 to 52 hours: 40 regular hours plus 12 of overtime. Implementation was phased by company size from 2018, with sectoral exceptions. The policy does not establish that every worker’s actual hours fell uniformly.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Peace advocacy and visits after office
strings.highlights.h2.text: At a National Assembly commemoration on 18 September 2026 he advocated renewed peninsula dialogue and military de-escalation. On 10 November he visited Gunsan with Kim Jung-sook, met former aides, toured a shipyard and walked an island trail. Later itinerary items in the report remain plans; his statements are not decisions already implemented by the incumbent government.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Indicted over allegations involving his former son-in-law’s employment
strings.timeline.t1.text: Prosecutors alleged that roughly 217 million won in pay and other benefits from Thai Eastar Jet to his former son-in-law amounted to benefits conveyed to Moon. His side disputed the accusations and criticized political prosecution. A 17 November 2026 report confirmed continuing pretrial proceedings, with a citizen-participation trial planned from 11 January 2027. A possible verdict on 22 January is conditional, not an existing conviction.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Pyeongsan Bookstore opens
strings.timeline.t2.text: He became involved in the bookstore in Pyeongsan village, Yangsan, South Gyeongsang Province, welcoming readers, selling books and recommending reading as a volunteer bookseller. A foundation established it, with management through a committee including residents. His daily participation does not make him sole proprietor or foundation chair.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Presidential term ends
strings.timeline.t3.text: On the final day of his five-year term he delivered a farewell address calling for continued inter-Korean dialogue. Yoon Suk-yeol succeeded him the next day. Moon subsequently held former-president status; continued public comment did not extend his presidential term.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Signing the Pyongyang Joint Declaration
strings.timeline.t4.text: During the 18–20 September inter-Korean summit in Pyongyang, he and Kim Jong-un signed a joint declaration incorporating a military implementation agreement as an annex. They proposed measures to reduce confrontation and expand exchanges. Signing commitments, implementing them and achieving durable peace are separate stages.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Issuing the Panmunjom Declaration with Kim Jong-un
strings.timeline.t5.text: Following talks at Panmunjom’s Peace House, the two sides set shared goals of improving relations, reducing military tensions and pursuing peninsula denuclearization, while seeking a peace regime. The declaration was a political commitment, not an already concluded peace treaty ending the war or proof of completed nuclear disarmament.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Taking office as South Korean president
strings.timeline.t6.text: He won the presidential election on 9 May and took office with an inaugural address on 10 May. The Presidential Archives records his as the 19th presidency. Election and inauguration dates are distinct; the numbered presidency is not the count of individual officeholders.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Elected to parliament and contests the presidency
strings.timeline.t7.text: He won the Busan Sasang parliamentary seat and served until 2016. In 2012 he ran for president for the Democratic United Party, losing to Park Geun-hye. His 2012 candidacy and his 2017 victory belong to separate elections.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Beginning legal collaboration with Roh Moo-hyun
strings.timeline.t8.text: He worked with Roh Moo-hyun in Busan on legal services focused on human rights and labour cases. His early legal practice and democracy activism shaped his political background. Passing the judicial examination in 1980 and later serving as a presidential aide were separate milestones.
